newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus aristata seed cones as 6–11 cm long, spreading and symmetric; before opening they are lance-cylindric, and when open they are lance-ovoid to ovoid or cylindric, with strongly thickened apophyses.
newRecords.caveat: The account also notes a flattened crown form as sheared; that horticultural wording is not treated here as a natural crown trait.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus banksiana seed cones as 3–5.5 cm long; most apophyses are depressed and become increasingly mammillate toward the outer cone base.
requiredSourceText: increasingly mammillate toward outer cone base
newRecords.caveat: The account separately mentions long-serotinous cones and seed release with age or fire; this morphology claim does not recast those behaviors as habitat or general ecology.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus contorta seed cones as variable in shape and symmetry, 2–6 cm long, and broadly ovoid to nearly globose when open; their apophyses are nearly rhombic and cross-keeled.
requiredSourceText: broadly ovoid to nearly globose when open
newRecords.caveat: The source explicitly reports variation and states that its chromosome count is not assigned to a variety; neither is generalized beyond the account.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus coulteri seed cones as asymmetric at the base and 20–35 cm long; their apophyses and umbos form long, upcurved claws 2.5–3 cm long.
newRecords.caveat: Dimensions are account-level descriptive bounds, not population means or a statement about how often the largest cones occur.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus edulis seed cones as about 3.5–5 cm long, symmetric, ovoid before opening, and depressed-ovoid to nearly globose when open.
requiredSourceText: depressed-ovoid to nearly globose when open
newRecords.caveat: The account gives a taxonomic description, not a population sampling frame or frequency distribution.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus engelmannii seed cones as 11–14 cm long, lance-ovoid before opening and ovoid when open; the apophyses are rhombic and strongly cross-keeled.
newRecords.caveat: The account-level description does not report population means or variation across the complete COL26.8 concept.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus flexilis seed cones as 7–15 cm long, lance-ovoid before opening and cylindro-ovoid when open, with much-thickened, strongly cross-keeled apophyses.
newRecords.caveat: Dimensions and shape are limited to the cited flora account and are not population estimates.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus lambertiana seed cones as symmetric and 25–50 cm long, cylindric before opening and lance-cylindric to ellipsoid-cylindric when open.
newRecords.caveat: These are descriptive bounds in one regional flora account, not population means.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus monophylla seed cones as 4–6 cm long, occasionally to 8 cm; they are ovoid before opening and broadly depressed-ovoid to nearly globose when open.
requiredSourceText: broadly depressed-ovoid to nearly globose when open
newRecords.caveat: The reported range is from an account-level description, not a population frequency estimate.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus palustris seed cones as 15–25 cm long, lanceoloid before opening and ovoid-cylindric when open; their apophyses are strongly cross-keeled.
newRecords.caveat: These account-level descriptors do not state the frequency or population distribution of cone sizes.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus radiata seed cones as 7–14 cm long, very asymmetric, and broadly ovoid when open, with rigid scales.
newRecords.caveat: This is a North American flora account, not a worldwide range or cultivation assessment; size is an account-level descriptive range.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus attenuata seed cones as very asymmetric and 8–15 cm long, lanceoloid before opening and ovoid-cylindric when open.
newRecords.caveat: The source separately describes serotiny and fire-related opening; those behaviors are not included in this morphology claim.
